course_name_original: SEGURIDAD Y SALUD EN EL TRABAJO
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Occupational Safety and Health, risk identification and preventive measures

learning_outcomes.text: Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial areas, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Organization and planning of projects and human teams. Teamwork and leadership ability.
Knowledge of occupational safety and industrial hygiene as well as the ability for their practical application.

syllabus_topics: UNIT 1, 2, 3 Safety and Health. Generalities. Legislation. Occupational safety and health, generalities. Accident statistics. Preventive techniques. Preventive study of Regulations: Occupational Risk Prevention Law.
UNIT 4. Risk assessment. Methodology of occupational risk assessment, phases and types. Risk management. Practical cases.
UNIT 5. Safety and Health in construction works. Regulations. Safety and Health Studies. Occupational risk prevention plans. Elaboration.
UNIT 6: Work equipment. Use of Work Equipment. Machine protection. Risk prevention in work equipment. Degrees of protection, hazard elements. R.D. 1215/1997 and R.D. 1644/2008.
UNIT 7: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Safety signage, Work areas.

UNIT 9: Electrical risks at work. Safety in electrical maneuvers. Live working. Installations. Protections against direct and indirect electrical contacts. Authorized and Qualified Worker. R.D. 614/2001.
UNIT 10, 11, 12: Industrial hygiene. Ventilation, Chemical, Biological, Carcinogenic Contaminants, Asbestos.
UNIT 13: Industrial hygiene. Evaluation and control of industrial noise, Vibrations and Thermal Stress.
UNIT 14: Accident Investigation Problems and practical cases.
assessment_rules: The course can be passed by successfully completing the progressive evaluations, or by passing the global test in the ordinary call, or by passing the extraordinary call exam. For progressive evaluation, the average of two progressive written exams must be at least 5.0 out of 10, with a minimum of 4.0 in each exam. For the ordinary call global test, students who did not pass any progressive evaluation must score at least 5.0 out of 10 on a 40-question multiple-choice exam. Students who passed one progressive evaluation will take a 40-question multiple-choice exam on the unpassed material, needing at least 5.0, with the final grade being the average of the passed progressive evaluation and this global test. Extraordinary call follows the same rules as the ordinary call global test.
